CODE
221
Each spouse contributes to the expenses of the marriage according to his or her means.
If one of the spouses fails to fulfil this obligation, the other spouse may, [1 without it being necessary to prove fault and]1 without prejudice to the rights of third parties, be authorised by the [1 family court]1 to collect, to the exclusion of his or her spouse, under the conditions and within the limits set by the judgment, his or her income or that of the property he or she administers under their matrimonial property regime, as well as any other sums owed to him or her by third parties.
In no case shall the delegation of sums be granted to a spouse convicted of an act referred to in articles 375, 398 to 400, 402, 403 or 405 of the Penal Code, committed against the person of the defendant, or of an attempt to commit an act referred to in articles 375, 393, 394 or 397 of the same Code against that same person.]1
The judgment may be set up against all current or future third-party debtors upon notification to them by the court clerk at the request of the plaintiff.
When the judgment ceases to have effect, the third-party debtors are informed by the Registrar.
